newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO delegation to U.S. to discuss peace.
newsitem.headline: PLO delegation to U.S. to discuss peace.

text.p: A Palestinian delegation planned to travel to Washington on Wednesday for talks with U.S. officials on launching an American initiative to save the Middle East peace process, a PLO official said.

The visit by PLO chief negotiator Mahmoud Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen, and negotiator Saeb Erekat will follow White House talks on Monday between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. President Bill Clinton.

"Abu Mazen and I will leave for Washington tonight upon invitation by the U.S. administration for consultation with U.S. officials on American efforts to launch an American initiative to save the peace process," Erekat told Reuters.
Clinton on Tuesday said he believed there was a "fairly decent chance" of reviving peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians.

Violence has flared almost daily in the West Bank since Israel broke ground for a Jewish housing project in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 which Palestinians charged completed a ring of Israeli settlements on disputed land around the city.

Erekat said points that any American proposal should include for it to succeed were ..."the reiteration that the peace process is based on exchange of land for peace, and final status talks should be conducted parallel to implementation of interim issues."

Netanyahu has proposed moving directly into accelerated talks on a permanent peace accord with the PLO which would deal with "final-status" issues such as the future of Jerusalem and settlements Israel has built on occupied land.

"It is imperative that Israel refrain from undertaking unilateral actions such as building settlements and land confiscations. There is no peace with settlements and no peace with violence," Erekat said.
Netanyahu has vowed to continue building at Har Homa, called Jabal Abu Ghneim by Palestinians, and in other settlements.
But he insisted on Tuesday -- the bloodiest day of West Bank violence since bulldozers began to move at the East Jerusalem site -- that peace could still be salvaged.

Israeli soldiers and settlers shot dead three Palestinians and wounded scores in the West Bank town of Hebron on Tuesday. Erekat said Israel must immediately disarm settlers, charging they instigate violence.
"I believe there is a way to move forward," Netanyahu told foreign reporters after returning home from Washington.
Netanyahu said he had put forward ideas to break the political deadlock and end Palestinian street protests.
"I heard other ideas..from President Clinton," Netanyahu said without elaborating.
